analysis: All three changed files are test-only (ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD): SSDHybridCheckpointStoreTests.swift (new test at head lines 206-240), SSDPrefixCacheTelemetryTests.swift (comment-only change at head lines 181-182), and SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (test helper refactor plus new write-behind queue-bound tests). No production source is modified in the supplied evidence, so there is no new attack surface, no change to crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, disk budget, cacheSalt scoping, or staging-reservation paths from T-041. The new tests assert existing availability and bounding behavior of the write-behind pipeline. They check that six jobs queue and a seventh settles as write_queue_full, that the queued-byte cap is enforced, that a job admitted while its predecessor settles is not dropped, and that a refused conversation's blocks are released so it can retry. These exercise the T-041 mitigation for bounded transient RAM in the donation pipeline and the fallback-to-recompute posture. Test helpers use SymmetricKey(size:.bits256) randomly generated keys and temp dirs, with no secret material or real keys. The tests rely on production symbols such as acceptedCount, droppedCount, afterPublishBeforeIndexForTesting, startDonation, SSDDonationSubmitResult, submitWithResult, writeQueueMaxJobs and waitForWritesForTesting. The corresponding non-test changes are not in this batch, so I could not verify them. If the PR adds testing hooks or loosens the writer gate or buffer depth in production code, that should be reviewed against T-041 detection hints (write-behind bounds, staging release paths). From this test-only batch alone, no security regression is identified.
